_metadata.description: Real Two-Line Element (TLE) database for major spacecraft
notes: TLEs are snapshots valid near their epoch date.
Positions propagated from these elements accumulate error over time.
For current positions, fetch live data from CelesTrak or Space-Track.
All NORAD catalog numbers from https://celestrak.org/satcat/search.php

satellites.name: ISS (ZARYA)
satellites.description: The International Space Station — humanity's permanent orbital laboratory since 2000. Maintained by NASA, Roscosmos, ESA, JAXA, and CSA.
satellites.notes: Altitude maintained between 400–420 km via periodic reboosts. Inclination chosen to allow access from Baikonur Cosmodrome.

satellites.name: HUBBLE SPACE TELESCOPE
satellites.description: NASA/ESA space telescope launched 1990 aboard STS-31. Revolutionized astronomy with images from UV to near-IR.
satellites.notes: Low inclination due to launch from Kennedy Space Center (latitude 28.5°). Serviced five times by Space Shuttle crews.

satellites.name: JWST
satellites.description: James Webb Space Telescope at Sun-Earth L2. Observes in infrared 1–28 µm. Launched Ariane 5 VA256.
satellites.notes: Not in a true Keplerian orbit around Earth — TLE shown is an approximation for visualisation. JWST performs a halo orbit around L2, ~1.5 M km from Earth.

satellites.name: STARLINK-1007
satellites.description: First operational Starlink v1.0 broadband internet satellite (SpaceX). Shell 1 at 550 km, 53° inclination.
satellites.notes: SpaceX Starlink constellation had >6 000 satellites by 2026 in multiple shells at 340–570 km.

satellites.name: STARLINK-5678
satellites.description: Starlink v2 Mini satellite in 43° inclination shell for mid-latitude broadband coverage.
satellites.notes: v2 Mini satellites weigh ~800 kg vs ~260 kg for v1.0.

satellites.name: GPS BIIR-2  (PRN 13)
satellites.description: GPS Block IIR-2 navigation satellite. Part of the 24-satellite GPS constellation in 6 orbital planes.
satellites.notes: GPS uses L1 (1575.42 MHz) and L2 (1227.60 MHz) signals. Constellation designed for ≥4 SVs visible from any point.

satellites.name: GPS BIIF-10 (PRN 08)
satellites.description: GPS Block IIF-10 satellite, the 10th of 12 Block IIF satellites. Provides L1/L2/L5 signals.
satellites.notes: Block IIF added L5 signal (1176.45 MHz) for improved accuracy and aviation safety applications.

satellites.name: GOES 18
satellites.description: GOES-18 (GOES-West) geostationary weather satellite at 137°W. Replaced GOES-17 as operational GOES-West on Jan 4, 2023.
satellites.notes: NOAA GOES-R series provides visible and infrared imagery every 5–15 min with 0.5 km resolution.

satellites.name: GOES 16
satellites.description: GOES-16 (GOES-East) geostationary weather satellite at 75.2°W. First of the GOES-R series, operational since Dec 2017.
satellites.notes: ABI (Advanced Baseline Imager) provides 16-channel spectral imaging every 10 minutes full disk.

satellites.name: MOLNIYA 3-50
satellites.description: Russian Molniya 3 communications satellite in the classic 12-hour Molniya orbit (63.4° inclination, high eccentricity).
satellites.notes: 63.4° inclination is the critical inclination where the argument of perigee does not precess due to J2. Satellite spends ~8 hours per orbit over Russia/Arctic region near apogee.

satellites.name: SENTINEL-2A
satellites.description: ESA Sentinel-2A multispectral Earth-observation satellite at 786 km SSO. 13-band imager, 10 m resolution, 5-day revisit (with Sentinel-2B).
satellites.notes: SSO retrograde inclination (98.57°) causes orbital plane to precess ~1°/day eastward in step with Earth's orbit around the Sun.

satellites.name: LANDSAT 9
satellites.description: Landsat 9 — USGS/NASA Earth-observation satellite, continuing a data record since 1972. Carries OLI-2 and TIRS-2 instruments.
satellites.notes: Phased 8-day apart from Landsat 8 to achieve 8-day repeat coverage of all global land areas.

satellites.name: NOAA 20
satellites.description: NOAA-20 (JPSS-1) — primary operational weather satellite. VIIRS, CrIS, ATMS, OMPS instruments provide global weather data twice daily.
satellites.notes: Part of the Joint Polar Satellite System (JPSS) program replacing legacy NOAA POES satellites.

satellites.name: SOHO
satellites.source: NASA JPL Horizons (derived elements for visualisation)
satellites.description: Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO) at the Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange point. Provides uninterrupted solar wind and CME monitoring.
satellites.notes: Launched on Atlas IIAS. Has operated since 1996, far exceeding its original 2-year design life. TLE is approximate for visualisation only.

satellites.name: INTEGRAL
satellites.description: ESA INTEGRAL (INTErnational Gamma-Ray Astrophysics Laboratory). High-inclination elliptical orbit keeps it above the Van Allen belts >90% of its orbit for uninterrupted observations.
satellites.notes: 64-hour orbit period. Perigee passes through radiation belts; observations paused during belt crossings.

satellites.name: TERRA
satellites.description: NASA Terra (EOS-AM) Earth-observing satellite. Carries MODIS, ASTER, MISR, MOPITT, and CERES instruments for comprehensive climate monitoring.
satellites.notes: Descending node at 10:30 local solar time. Part of the A-Train constellation (Aqua, Aura, CloudSat, CALIPSO, PARASOL).

satellites.name: DSCOVR
satellites.source: NASA JPL Horizons (derived elements for visualisation)
satellites.description: NOAA Deep Space Climate Observatory (DSCOVR) at L1. Provides solar-wind measurements for space-weather forecasting. Carries EPIC camera with daily full-disk Earth imagery.
satellites.notes: TLE is approximate for visualisation only. Maintains a Lissajous orbit around L1.
